progressionAudit.Sets: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — no prior grade treats a set as an object with operations
progressionAudit.RelationsAndFunctions: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — relation and function as objects; prior grades used function-like rules without naming them
progressionAudit.TrigonometricFunctions: REPRESENTATION_EXTENSION plus NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — Class 10 Ch8 established acute right-triangle ratios in degrees; radian measure, the unit circle, signs by quadrant and functions over the reals are new. This is NOT first trigonometry.
progressionAudit.ComplexNumbers: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — motivated by Class 10 quadratics with negative discriminant, which Class 10 declared to have no real roots
progressionAudit.LinearInequalities: PROCEDURAL_EXTENSION — extends linear equation solving from Class 9 and 10 to an order relation
progressionAudit.PermutationsAndCombinations: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — systematic counting has no prior-grade equivalent
progressionAudit.BinomialTheorem: PROCEDURAL_EXTENSION plus PROOF_DEEPENING — Class 8 and 9 expanded squares and cubes; the general theorem with a proof is new
progressionAudit.SequencesAndSeries: PROCEDURAL_EXTENSION — Class 10 Ch5 derived the AP nth term and both sum forms; G.P. is a NEW_NAMED_OBJECT within an established frame
progressionAudit.StraightLines: PROCEDURAL_EXTENSION — Class 10 Ch7 gave distance and internal section; slope and line equations extend that coordinate frame
progressionAudit.ConicSections: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — no prior-grade curve beyond the Class 10 parabola as a polynomial graph
progressionAudit.ThreeDimensionalGeometry: REPRESENTATION_EXTENSION — the Class 10 coordinate plane extended to space; the distance formula generalises
progressionAudit.LimitsAndDerivatives: NEW_NAMED_OBJECT — no prior-grade limit or rate-of-change concept
progressionAudit.Statistics: PROCEDURAL_EXTENSION — Class 10 Ch13 did grouped mean, mode and median; dispersion is the new measure family
progressionAudit.Probability: FORMALISATION — Class 9 Ch7 and Class 10 Ch14 established sample space, equally likely outcomes and classical probability; the axiomatic set-theoretic treatment formalises it. Probability is NOT new.

a counting model distinct from the finite sample space model
